Working in /opt/nxeon-v2 (Next.js app, branch design/v2, a hosting platform). This is a WRITE task — make real code changes. This is going to production soon, so match the existing codebase's precise style and don't guess at things you can verify by reading.

CONTEXT: A rewrite of the deploy wizard (`components/nx/DeployView.tsx`, ~1863 lines, handles VPS/hosting/game/email orders — replacing the old per-product wizards `components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx`, `GameDeployWizard.tsx`, `HostingDeployWizard.tsx` which are now dead code for live traffic) dropped two things a prior audit found:

**Fix 1 — Deploy funnel step tracking is completely missing from DeployView.tsx.**
The old wizards called functions from `lib/deploy-funnel-client.ts` (`trackDeployStep`/`trackDeployError` or similarly named — READ that file first to get the exact exported function names/signatures) at meaningful step transitions. Read the OLD wizard files (`components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx`, `components/customer/GameDeployWizard.tsx`, `components/customer/HostingDeployWizard.tsx`) to see EXACTLY where and how they call these functions — what step names/labels they pass, and at which UI transitions (e.g. plan selected, moved to payment step, order submitted, order errored). Then add equivalent calls into `components/nx/DeployView.tsx` at the equivalent transitions, for ALL FOUR product types it now handles (vps/game/hosting/email) — reuse the exact same step-name strings the old wizards used per product where applicable, so `app/admin/deploy-funnel`'s existing aggregation queries (which key off those strings) keep working without needing their own changes. Check `lib/deploy-funnel.ts` and `app/admin/deploy-funnel/page.tsx` if you need to confirm what step-name values the admin dashboard actually expects/aggregates.

**Fix 2 — Game server region selection is entirely cosmetic.**
The wizard shows a region picker and displays the chosen region in the order summary for game orders, but `DeployView.tsx` never actually submits a `region` field in the game order's form data, and `lib/game-order.ts`'s `placeGameOrder`/`scheduleNode(quote.ramMB)` call (around line 419-444) never filters by region at all. Compare against how the VPS/Cloud-Hosting path in the SAME file already does this correctly (search `DeployView.tsx` for how it submits `region` for the VPS path, and how `lib/order.ts`'s `placeOrder` reads `intent.region` and passes it to `scheduleNode(planRamMB, { region, provider })` — mirror that exact pattern). You'll need to: (a) add a hidden `region` input to the game order's submitted form fields in `DeployView.tsx`, matching the VPS path's approach, (b) read that region in `lib/game-order.ts`'s intent-parsing function (find wherever `GameOrderIntent` is built from form data, likely near where `placeGameOrder` is called or in a `gameIntentFromFormData`-style function — search for how the VPS equivalent, `intentFromFormData` in `lib/order.ts`, does this) and add a `region` field to `GameOrderIntent`'s type if it doesn't have one, (c) pass that region into the `scheduleNode()` call the same way `lib/order.ts` does.

**Fix 3 — Mount the missing page-view tracker.**
`components/nx/Shell.tsx` (the shell every dashboard page renders inside) never mounts `<VisitTracker kind="portal" />`, unlike the old `components/portal/Shell.tsx` which does (search for exactly where and how `components/portal/Shell.tsx` renders it, and the import path). Add the equivalent to `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, matching the same import and usage pattern exactly. This is the single most impactful fix here — the entire dashboard's page-view analytics have been silently dead since this shell shipped.

After each fix, run `cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && npx tsc --noEmit` and resolve any type errors before moving on. Do not touch files outside `components/nx/DeployView.tsx`, `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, `lib/game-order.ts`, and whatever type-definition file `GameOrderIntent` lives in (likely also `lib/game-order.ts`). Do not commit — leave changes unstaged for review. Report back file-by-file with line numbers of what you changed and why, including the exact step-name strings you used for the funnel tracking so they can be cross-checked against the admin dashboard.

This file is the operating manual; that one is the direction and the history of what has been built. --- ## Where you are, and what that changes This tree runs on **node-2** (`nxeon-fsn1`, `178.63.94.114`), and the work is meant to happen there. Check which box you are on before anything else: ```bash hostname # nxeon-fsn1 = node-2. Anything else = the primary node. ``` **On node-2 (`nxeon-fsn1`) — the normal case.** Edit here and build here: ```bash npx tsc --noEmit # always, before a build ./rebuild.sh # stop, build, restart. ~125s. ``` **On the PRIMARY node.** Do not build. A `next build` there competes with paying customers for CPU. Edit if you must, then: ```bash scripts/deploy-node2.sh # ships the commit, typechecks + builds ON node-2 ``` It refuses to run on a dirty tree (it ships commits, not a working directory) and refuses to reset over commits node-2 has and the primary doesn't. **One source of truth at a time.** The deploy script does `git reset --hard` on node-2. Schema changes: `npm run db:push`. There are no migration files. The primary node and node-2 have **separate** `nxeon_v2` databases, so a push on one does nothing to the other. ## Reaching node-1 (live production) from here node-2 has **root SSH to node-1**, granted by the owner on 2026-09-11, because three things a Nexion session needs live only there: the board concept attachments (~500 MB across ~99 cards — the design source of truth), the production database (for checking a claim against real data instead of sandbox seed data), and the real production tree to compare the fork against. This supersedes the "treat it as read-only, ask first" rule that used to sit here — the routine build/deploy/promote path no longer needs a stop-and-ask. That authorization carries guardrails that are **not optional**: - **Take a fresh, named `pg_dump` snapshot immediately before any write to the prod DB**, the same discipline already used for the pre-merge backup (`pre--.dump` under `/root/db-backups` on node-1, pulled down to node-2 too). The authorization is for shipping this fork to production, not a blanket lift of every caution on this box. ## Rules that are not negotiable 1. **Never fabricate.** No invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, ETAs or capabilities. If a number cannot be read from the database or from a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why. This tree has already had hash-derived star ratings and fake customer reviews removed once — do not reintroduce that shape. There is a login-and-capture script: ```bash node scripts/shot.mjs /tmp/out /dashboard/directory /dashboard/settings # defaults to the design customer account; override with NX_EMAIL / NX_PASS ``` Playwright scripts must live inside `/opt/nxeon-v2` so the module resolves. Let the layout place things. - **`mask-composite` is unevenly supported** — nest two single-axis masks. - **An `` that fails before hydration never fires `onError`.** Check `el.complete && el.naturalWidth === 0` on mount. - **`fetch` cannot report request-body progress in any browser.** Upload progress needs `XMLHttpRequest.upload.onprogress`. - **Shell-level React providers are easy to drop.** The Nexion shell omitted `ComposeProvider`, then `TerminalDockProvider`, then `MatrixProvider` — each took a whole feature down invisibly, because the crash only appears on a route a smoke test does not walk. Anything added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` must be added to `components/nx/Shell.tsx` too. ## Conventions inherited from the platform (still true here) - Every VM state change goes through a `Job` row. The web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly. - One in-flight job per server. - Wallet amounts are integer cents. - Admin-only actions call `requireAdmin()` and refuse to render while impersonating. - Charts are dependency-free SVG in `components/ui/charts.tsx`. Do not add a charting library. ## Inherited instructions that do NOT apply here The production `CLAUDE.md` this replaced is kept at `docs/CLAUDE-production-inherited.md` for reference. It describes the PRIMARY node. To avoid a very expensive mistake: - **Do not** run `systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — that is production. This tree's unit is `nxeon-v2-web`. - **Do not** publish docs to `revsports.ca/docs` from here. - ~~Do not run `scripts/promote-production.sh` or `scripts/deploy-staging.sh`~~ — **superseded 2026-09-12.** The owner authorized running these directly from this session; see the guardrails in "Reaching node-1" above. - There is no post-commit auto-push hook on node-2, and there should not be: `design/v2` is a design fork, not something to push to `origin` casually.
